verdict.label: apparent_contradiction
verdict.rationale: Both abstracts report an association between circulating irisin and fasting plasma glucose, but with opposite directions: in Taiwanese schoolchildren, irisin was negatively related to FPG in boys (r = -0.21, P = .006) after age adjustment, whereas in T2DM/MAFLD patients, lower irisin was associated with lower FPG (i.e., a positive relationship). The populations differ substantially (healthy children vs. adults with T2DM and MAFLD), which is a concrete, source-supported contextual difference that could explain the opposite findings.

source_evidence.quote: After adjusting for age, the irisin level in boys was negatively related to fasting plasma glucose (FPG) (r = -0.21, P = .006).
those with a lower level of irisin showed lower WHR, FPG and FINS levels

diagnostics.notes: Side A: negative irisin-FPG association in boys (children, Taiwan). Side B: lower irisin with lower FPG in T2DM/MAFLD patients, implying a positive association. Opposite directions with a clear population difference (healthy schoolchildren vs. adults with T2DM and MAFLD).
